title: Gacha Simulation: Understanding Pity Mechanics and Probability Psychology
subtitle: This article deconstructs the structural differences between hard and soft pity systems, analyzing how probability psychology creates perceptual bias. Through simulation verification of gacha data, we reveal the impact of emotional thresholds on decision-making. This helps developers quantify the risks of pity strategies and optimize numerical design to enhance user retention and willingness to pay.

breakdown.title: Pity Structure (Most Common)
bullets: Hard Pity: Guaranteed drop of target rarity after N pulls
Soft Pity: Probability increases as you approach N (feels better)
Directed Mechanism: Big pity/Warp system ensures a guaranteed drop on the next pull if missed, reducing the feeling of being 'backstabbed'

breakdown.title: Probability Psychology
bullets: Players remember 'streaks of failure', not the mean
Soft pity significantly reduces the tail probability of long failure streaks
Clearly writing the rules can actually reduce controversy (players fear the 'black box')

breakdown.title: Simulation and Verification
bullets: Look at the distribution, not just the expectation: How many pulls for P50/P90/P99
Compare 'Pure Random vs. Soft Pity' to observe the proportion of extreme 'chump' cases
Monitor churn points: Retention drops when consecutive failures exceed a threshold
